source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Mineral Nutrition
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Arnon and Stout’s criteria of essentiality require that the element is needed for
options: normal growth and is not replaceable by another element
questions.explanation: An essential element is required for the life cycle, has a specific role, and cannot be substituted.

questions.stem: Calcium is a macronutrient mainly required as a constituent of the
questions.explanation: Calcium pectate cements the middle lamella; magnesium, not calcium, sits in chlorophyll.

questions.stem: Molybdenum is required in plants mainly because it is a component of
questions.explanation: Mo is a cofactor of nitrate reductase and of nitrogenase, so it is vital for nitrogen metabolism.

questions.stem: Whiptail of cauliflower is a deficiency disorder linked to
questions.explanation: Mo deficiency produces narrow, distorted ‘whip’ leaves in cauliflower.

questions.stem: Julius von Sachs demonstrated mineral needs of plants by growing them in
questions.explanation: Sachs pioneered solution culture; modern hydroponics is the same principle.

questions.stem: A free-living aerobic nitrogen-fixing bacterium commonly cited in textbooks is
questions.explanation: Azotobacter fixes N2 in aerobic soil; Rhizobium is symbiotic inside legume nodules.

questions.stem: Infection threads that carry rhizobia into the cortex are a step in
questions.explanation: After root-hair curling, an infection thread delivers rhizobia to cortical cells that become the nodule.

questions.stem: The pink pigment that buffers oxygen around bacteroids in a nodule is
questions.explanation: Leghaemoglobin keeps free O2 low so nitrogenase can work, while still supplying bound oxygen for respiration.

questions.stem: Transfer of an amino group from an amino acid to a keto acid is called
questions.explanation: Transaminases move −NH2 onto keto acids, spreading nitrogen into many amino acids.

questions.stem: Passive uptake of ions that later exchange according to Donnan equilibrium occurs mainly in the
options: apparent free space of the root
questions.explanation: Ions first enter the apoplast (apparent free space) passively; further uptake into the symplast is often active.

questions.stem: Deficiency of a mobile element such as nitrogen first appears in
questions.explanation: Mobile nutrients are remobilised from old leaves to growing points, so old leaves yellow first.

questions.stem: Anabaena living in the leaf cavities of Azolla is important in paddy fields because it
questions.explanation: The Azolla–Anabaena symbiosis adds fixed nitrogen to flooded rice soils.

questions.stem: Choose the correct combination. I. Carbon, hydrogen and oxygen are obtained mainly from CO2 and water, not as soil minerals. II. Nickel is now listed among essential micronutrients. III. All micronutrients are required in amounts greater than 10 mmol kg−1 dry matter.
questions.explanation: C, H, O come from air and water; Ni is essential (urease). Micronutrients are needed in far smaller amounts than that threshold.

questions.stem: An element is not considered essential if the plant can complete its life cycle when that element is
options: fully withheld and a substitute works equally well
questions.explanation: Essentiality fails if growth is normal without the element or if another ion can replace it completely.

questions.stem: Potassium as a macronutrient is especially important for
options: being the FeMo centre of nitrogenase
questions.explanation: K+ is the major osmotic ion of guard cells and activates many enzymes; it is not a chlorophyll constituent.

questions.stem: Iron is a micronutrient required because it
options: is the central atom of chlorophyll
is needed for chlorophyll synthesis and redox proteins
cements the middle lamella as pectate
is the only element in cellulose
questions.explanation: Fe is a cofactor in cytochromes and ferredoxin and is required to make chlorophyll, but Mg is the ring metal.

questions.stem: Little-leaf disease of apple is classically associated with deficiency of
questions.explanation: Zn deficiency produces little leaf / rosette in apple and other fruit trees.

questions.stem: In solution culture, aeration of the nutrient medium is needed mainly to
options: remove all nitrate from the tank
questions.explanation: Roots in waterlogged solution would otherwise suffer hypoxia; bubbling air keeps them aerobic.

questions.stem: Frankia forms nitrogen-fixing nodules on roots of
questions.explanation: Frankia is an actinomycete that nodulates actinorhizal hosts such as alder (Alnus).

questions.stem: Nod genes of Rhizobium are induced by plant-released
questions.explanation: Root flavonoids activate nodulation genes; the bacterium then makes Nod factors that curl the hair.

questions.stem: Nitrogenase converts N2 to ammonia and is a complex of
questions.explanation: The Mo-Fe protein (dinitrogenase) plus the Fe protein (reductase) together reduce N2 to NH3.

questions.stem: The GS–GOGAT pathway assimilates ammonia into
questions.explanation: Glutamine synthetase and glutamate synthase are the main route of NH4+ assimilation in plants.

questions.stem: Carrier-mediated ion uptake into root cells that can be saturated and is often energy-dependent is
options: purely apoplastic flow past the Casparian strip
active or facilitated transport at the plasma membrane
diffusion of O2 through aerenchyma only
questions.explanation: Ion carriers/channels in the plasmalemma show specificity and saturation; many steps are active.

questions.stem: Interveinal chlorosis of young leaves with veins remaining green is most typical of deficiency of
options: a mobile element such as nitrogen
an immobile micronutrient such as iron
questions.explanation: Fe is poorly remobilised, so young leaves show interveinal chlorosis while veins stay greener.

questions.stem: Which statement about nitrogenase is incorrect?
options: It needs a large ATP supply.
Leghaemoglobin helps protect it from free oxygen.
It functions best when the nodule is fully aerobic and free of any oxygen-binding protein.
questions.explanation: Nitrogenase is O2-labile; the nodule is microaerobic and uses leghaemoglobin, not a fully aerobic unprotected state.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect match of element and principal role.
options: Boron — pollen-tube growth and membrane function
Magnesium — central metal of the middle lamella pectate
questions.explanation: Mg is the central atom of chlorophyll and an enzyme cofactor; calcium pectate forms the middle lamella.
